blocks.text: Parents in Japan are taking an increasingly active role in their children’s lives, helping them find marriage partners, navigate job hunting and secure housing, as the line between parental support and personal decision-making continues to blur. In a practice known as “proxy matchmaking,” parents attend social events armed with photos and profiles of their children, hoping to find suitable marriage partners through conversations with other parents. The Association of Parents of Marriage Proposal Information, which began organizing such gatherings in 2005, says attendance has grown from a few dozen people to around 200 at events in major cities, while regional gatherings […]...
